title.narrative: Empowering Women Economically through the Digitalization of VSLA in Juba County, Central Equatoria State

description.narrative: The years of conflicts, compounded by the impact of climatic shocks and food insecurity, have heightened the humanitarian situation and limited the development of some of the most vulnerable groups, such as women and girls in Juba County of Central Equatoria state. While women have enormous potential to contribute to building resilience and elevating their socio–economic status, they face significant challenges to economic empowerment due to limited access to financial services, education and technology. Women and young women also have limited opportunities to support themselves, given the high rates of economic vulnerability, illiteracy, pervasive gender social norms that hinder their access to livelihood opportunities, including land and economic justice. The sustained insecurity in South Sudan has left many women and girls as head of households and sole breadwinners with few options to provide for themselves and their families. As the cost-of-living soars and livelihood remains unstable, the burden of poverty and economic violence weighs heavily on women, and most have hardly enough money at their disposal to sustain their family households. As women take on the responsibility of household management and income generation by starting small businesses and organizing themselves in Traditional village saving and loan associations (VSLA) to save, borrow, and invest in income-generating activities. However, group members often face security risks for their physical cash in the savings boxes, and limitations in financial literacy, and access to broader financial credits from the bank. Thereby, NWERO leadership believe, “if the marginalized and vulnerable women are provided customized economic empowerment skills through digitalized village saving and loan association, including financial literacy, then their income significantly increases, and they will have a sustainable livelihood and peace in their households.
